clue.text: Firm restricted guests

parts.note: restricted means limited, kept within bounds
guests staying with you are your company

explanation.surface: A business keeps its guest list short.
explanation.definitionFit: A limited company is a type of business whose owners' liability is capped, so it is a firm.

clue.text: Lengthy split in schoolwork?

parts.note: lengthy means long
a split is a division

explanation.surface: A long split appears in a piece of school homework.
explanation.definitionFit: Long division is the written arithmetic method taught to pupils for dividing large numbers.

clue.text: Grumble about this hairdo

indicators.note: about means the grumble goes round the Latin word

parts.note: to grumble is to moan
hic is Latin for this

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mohican is a hairstyle with a central strip of upright hair and shaved sides.

clue.text: Attempt to include fancy wad that's cheap and showy

indicators.note: to include means the attempt holds the rearranged letters inside

parts.note: an attempt is a try

indicators.note: fancy means the letters of wad are arranged ornately into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tries to fit a flashy wad of cash into something cheap and gaudy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tawdry describes goods that are gaudy yet of poor quality, tacky.

clue.text: Be up in time for talk

indicators.note: in means the reversed letters sit inside the date

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: up means the word be is read upwards, backwards in a down answer

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to get up early enough for a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A debate is a formal discussion, a talk with arguments on both sides.

clue.text: One watches old boy, somebody in court

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a server is a player putting the ball into play on a tennis court

explanation.surface: A former pupil watches someone in a law court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court; here it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: An observer is a person who watches events without taking part.

clue.text: Angrily lets rip, welcoming answer in column

indicators.note: welcoming means the rearranged letters take the A inside them
angrily means the letters of lets rip are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone furiously rants while answering in a newspaper column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Column' looks like a newspaper feature; it is an architectural one.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilaster is a rectangular column projecting slightly from a wall.

clue.text: Greek character getting easy to understand type of energy

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
something easy to understand is clear

explanation.surface: A Greek person finds a type of energy simple to grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear energy is power released from atomic nuclei by fission or fusion.

clue.text: Not in any way having specialised skill reported

indicators.note: reported signals that we hear the words spoken rather than see them written

parts.note: specialised skill is know-how, practical expertise

explanation.surface: Someone denies, flatly, having any expertise at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Nohow is a dialect adverb meaning by no means, in no manner whatsoever.

clue.text: Church made by graduate with quartz

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
quartz is a crystalline form of silica, silicon dioxide

explanation.surface: A church built by a graduate out of quartz.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong church, often one granted special papal privileges.

clue.text: Magazine complains too violently

indicators.note: violently means the letters of complains too are thrashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A magazine reader protests far too strongly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmopolitan is a well-known women's glossy magazine title.

clue.text: On vacation, dance with Conservative speaker who might get plastered?

indicators.note: on vacation means the word dance is emptied, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker dances with a Tory speechmaker and might end up drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' looks like slang for drunk, which fits the party scene; here it means covered with plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorator renovates rooms and may apply plaster to walls, so he is someone who plasters.

clue.text: Diocese to make sure about

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A diocese is told to sort something out.
explanation.definitionFit: To see to something is the idiom for attending to it and ensuring it gets done.

clue.text: Means of escape secured by adventurer

indicators.note: secured by means held inside the word adventurer, which keeps these letters within it

explanation.surface: An adventurer has locked away his escape route.
explanation.definitionFit: A vent is an opening through which gas or liquid can get out, an outlet.

clue.text: Mrs Simpson maybe allowed to return message

indicators.note: to return means the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: Marge Simpson, of the cartoon The Simpsons, is one Mrs Simpson
allowed means let

explanation.surface: Mrs Simpson is permitted to reply to a message.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Simpson suggests Wallis Simpson, the royal divorcee; the 'maybe' points to another, Marge of The Simpsons.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram is a short message sent by telegraph.

clue.text: Profoundly involved but not up to one's neck

definitions.meaning: first meaning: deeply engaged in an activity or situation
second meaning: literally, submerged only as far as the knees

explanation.walkthrough: Up to one's neck is an idiom for deeply involved, so the clue seems to contradict itself; read literally, water at knee level is well below the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Being knee-deep in something is an idiom for heavy involvement, and literally means immersed only to the knees.

clue.text: Type of critic having no standing?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an ... critic comments without practical experience
second meaning: something you sit in, so not standing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Having no standing' reads as lacking authority, which fits a critic; it is also a jokey description of a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair critic judges from comfort without expertise; the chair itself is for sitting rather than upright posture.

clue.text: Second marine upset with year in college

indicators.note: upset means the letters of marine are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A marine, disturbed, spends a year at college.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminary is a college where priests are trained.

clue.text: More interesting, but not to vegetarians, perhaps

definitions.meaning: second meaning: containing more meat, which vegetarians would not find appealing

explanation.walkthrough: The 'but' joins the two meanings: richer in substance, and literally fuller of flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Meatier is used figuratively for something with more substance and literally for food with more flesh.

clue.text: Wind up good person before work

indicators.note: before places the saint ahead of the work

parts.note: ST, saint, is a crossword stock for a good person
OP, opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Annoy a virtuous person ahead of their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind up' looks like British slang for teasing; here it means bring to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind up a meeting is to finish or halt it, so it means come to a stop.

clue.text: Limits to public transport?

parts.note: the ends of bus or rail lines, where the routes stop, are their boundaries

explanation.walkthrough: 'Limits' suggests restrictions on travel; it means the endpoints of the routes.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway and bus stations at the end of a line are the end points, the places where routes finish.

clue.text: Places reversed — soldiers in a daze

indicators.note: reversed means the word for places is turned back to front

parts.note: places, as a verb, means puts
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers, their positions turned round, wander about confused.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a state of near-unconsciousness or dulled senses, a daze.

clue.text: Digestive spasm following fizz

indicators.note: following places the spasm after the fizz

parts.note: fizz, as liveliness, is pep
a tic is a spasm, an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A digestive spasm comes after drinking something fizzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Peptic relates to digestion, as in a peptic ulcer of the stomach.

clue.text: Egg-shaped container found in empty office

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the emptied office
empty means the word office loses its insides, keeping only its outer letters

parts.note: a vat is a large container for liquids

explanation.surface: An oval container turns up in a deserted office.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovate is a botanical term for oval with a broader base, like an egg's outline.

clue.text: Impressive building: see around it!

parts.note: an invitation to tour a grand building, with see also meaning a bishop's diocese, whose principal church this is

explanation.surface: A tourist is urged to look round a grand building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' reads as look, but a see is also a bishop's diocese, and the building is the centre of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is the principal church of a diocese, housing the bishop's throne, and is usually imposing.

clue.text: Dispensed with current measure for gas

parts.note: dispensed with someone's services means fired them
the amp is the unit measuring electric current

explanation.surface: A worker was sacked over a measurement for gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is the explosive methane mixture found in coal mines.

clue.text: Famous Dickensian dance?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Oliver ..., Dickens's orphan hero
second meaning: the ..., a 1960s rock and roll dance

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for a dance from a Dickens novel; it is two separate meanings of one surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of a Dickens character is also the name of a popular sixties dance craze.

clue.text: Rugby player confused ref with right move for three-quarters, say

parts.note: a prop is a front-row forward in rugby

indicators.note: confused means the letters of ref are muddled

parts.note: an action is a move, something done

explanation.surface: A rugby forward baffles the referee with a correct play for the three-quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby, three-quarters are backs, which fits the surface; here it is the number 3/4.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator, and 3/4 is an example.
